title: Roasted Sweet Potato–Oat Buns

items.text: 1 large orange-fleshed sweet potato (enough for 2 cups mashed)
2 cups roasted mashed sweet potato (from above)
1 container (5.3 oz) high-protein vanilla soy yogurt
1 tablespoon butter (if you feel like it)

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F. Scrub the sweet potato, leave the skin on, and pierce it several times with a fork. Roast on a baking sheet for 45–75 minutes, depending on size.
steps.donenessCue: A knife slides easily through the center.

steps.text: Cool until comfortable to handle, then peel and mash until completely smooth. Measure out 2 cups. Don’t add water, milk, or butter — you want its natural moisture and concentrated roasted flavor.
Warm the ¼ cup soy milk to about 105–110°F. Stir in the 2 tablespoons honey and 2¼ teaspoons yeast. Let sit 5–10 minutes.
Whisk together the 2 cups mashed sweet potato, 2 eggs, 5.3 oz vanilla soy yogurt, ¼ cup grapeseed oil, 2 tablespoons vanilla, and zest of 1 orange until smooth and uniform.

In a separate bowl, whisk the 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup whole-wheat flour, ½ cup oat flour, 2 teaspoons cinnamon, 1 teaspoon nutmeg, ½ teaspoon ginger, ¼ teaspoon allspice, and 1 teaspoon sea salt.

Pour the bloomed yeast into the wet sweet-potato mixture and stir. Add the combined wet mixture to the dry ingredients and stir until a shaggy dough forms. Don’t add extra flour right away — this dough should be soft and somewhat sticky.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface. Knead 6–8 minutes, adding flour only 1 tablespoon at a time if absolutely necessary.
steps.donenessCue: Soft, elastic, slightly tacky — not a stiff bread dough.

steps.text: Place in a lightly oiled bowl. Cover and let rise somewhere warm for 60–90 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Noticeably puffy and close to doubled.

steps.text: Mix the ¾ cup almond flour, 3 tablespoons softened butter, 2 tablespoons honey, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, ½ teaspoon vanilla, zest of ½ orange, and pinch of salt into a cohesive, spreadable paste. Fold in the ½ cup chopped pecans.
steps.donenessCue: Soft and spreadable, not crumbly. Too dry? Add another teaspoon of softened butter.

steps.text: Turn the risen dough onto a lightly floured surface. Gently roll into roughly a 12 × 18-inch rectangle. Don’t flatten aggressively — preserve the air.
Spread the filling evenly, leaving about ½ inch bare around the edges.
Starting from the long side, roll into a reasonably tight log. Pinch the seam closed.
Cut the log into 12 roughly equal pieces. Place each cut-side up in a lined standard muffin pan. They should fill about ½–⅔ of each cup.
Cover loosely and let rise 30–45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Bake 18–22 minutes, checking at 18.
steps.donenessCue: Tops lightly golden, centers set but still soft.

steps.text: While the buns bake, gently warm the 3 tablespoons honey, 1 tablespoon orange juice, 1 teaspoon orange zest, ½ teaspoon vanilla, and pinch of salt over low heat for 1–2 minutes, without boiling. Remove from heat and whisk in the 1 tablespoon butter, if using.
Cool the buns about 10 minutes, then drizzle with the warm glaze.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Skip the butter in the glaze for a lighter, more citrus-forward finish.
storage: Room temperature in an airtight container up to 2 days, or fridge up to 5 days. Freeze unglazed up to 2 months — thaw and glaze fresh. Reheat briefly in a low oven or microwave.
